classification.difficultyReason: Choose powers or inverse roots according to the given column, reconstruct ratios from terms supplied across different columns, and combine these relationships with algebraic index laws, including fractional exponents in the final row.

answer.worked:
Square and cube the length terms.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area ratio}&=5^2:3^2=25:9\\\text{Volume ratio}&=5^3:3^3=125:27\end{aligned}$$

The first length term is $1$, so its cube is $1$. Take cube roots of the volume terms, then square the length terms.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt[3]{1}:\sqrt[3]{1000}=1:10\\\text{Area ratio}&=1^2:10^2=1:100\\\text{Volume ratio}&=1:1000\end{aligned}$$

Recover the first length term from its square and the second from its cube.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt{16}:\sqrt[3]{27}=4:3\\\text{Area ratio}&=4^2:3^2=16:9\\\text{Volume ratio}&=4^3:3^3=64:27\end{aligned}$$

Take square roots of the area terms, then cube the length terms.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt{1}:\sqrt{0.01}=1:0.1\\\text{Volume ratio}&=1^3:0.1^3=1:0.001\end{aligned}$$

Take cube roots of the volume terms, then square the length terms.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt[3]{0.008}:\sqrt[3]{0.000001}\\\text{Length ratio}&=0.2:0.01\\\text{Area ratio}&=0.2^2:0.01^2=0.04:0.0001\end{aligned}$$

The area term $b^2$ gives length term $b$, and the volume term $c^3$ gives length term $c$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=a:b:c\\\text{Area ratio}&=a^2:b^2:c^2\\\text{Volume ratio}&=a^3:b^3:c^3\end{aligned}$$

The corresponding length terms are $2a$, $\sqrt{9b^2}=3b$ and $\sqrt[3]{64c^3}=4c$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=2a:3b:4c\\\text{Area ratio}&=(2a)^2:(3b)^2:(4c)^2\\\text{Area ratio}&=4a^2:9b^2:16c^2\\\text{Volume ratio}&=(2a)^3:(3b)^3:(4c)^3\\\text{Volume ratio}&=8a^3:27b^3:64c^3\end{aligned}$$

Square and cube each length term.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area ratio}&=(a^2)^2:(b^3)^2:(c^4)^2\\\text{Area ratio}&=a^4:b^6:c^8\\\text{Volume ratio}&=(a^2)^3:(b^3)^3:(c^4)^3\\\text{Volume ratio}&=a^6:b^9:c^{12}\end{aligned}$$

Take square roots of the area terms, then cube the length terms.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt a:\sqrt{b^2}:\sqrt{c^3}\\\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt a:b:c^{3/2}\\\text{Volume ratio}&=(a^{1/2})^3:b^3:(c^{3/2})^3\\\text{Volume ratio}&=a^{3/2}:b^3:c^{9/2}\end{aligned}$$

inlines.text: Square each length term for the area ratio and cube each length term for the volume ratio. Use square or cube roots to work backwards.
